Population.evidence_source: A total of 10 participants, consisting of 4 women aged 21–45 years and 6 men aged 25–52 years, were selected and asked to participate by a psychology specialist in connection with a follow-up after suicide attempts. In addition to serious suicidal tendencies or an actual suicide attempt, the ability to verbalize experiences was an inclusion criterion for participation.

Type.evidence_source: A total of 10 participants, consisting of 4 women aged 21–45 years and 6 men aged 25–52 years, were selected and asked to participate by a psychology specialist in connection with a follow-up after suicide attempts. The interview was to be carried out at the earliest 2 weeks after the emergency situation, and the participant was to have an offer from a treatment person at least 2 weeks after the completion of the interview.

Area.evidence_source: Several of them had had recent break-ups with partners. Five were on sick leave from permanent employment, one of them still working. Three participants were on disability insurance, and two were in the educational system. Several of the participants had had previous contact with psychiatric healthcare. For two of the younger participants, the suicide attempt led them to the first meeting with the support services. Suicide was attempted by consuming various doses and types of medicines; four had combined overdosing with alcohol. Forced hospitalization prevented one participant with a well thought out suicide plan from carrying it out. The person in question and four other participants were followed up in the emergency psychiatric ward, while the other five were followed up by a crisis resolution team in a regional psychiatric centre. The interview was to be carried out at the earliest 2 weeks after the emergency situation, and the participant was to have an offer from a treatment person at least 2 weeks after the completion of the interview.
